dossier.public_summary: The dip is shallow and only seen in 2 of 3 sectors at very different depths, with individual transits not matching each other. Four nearby stars bright enough to mimic the signal exist within one TESS pixel and the light curve shows strong spot variability. This pattern is best explained by a blend or noise, not a 3.4 Earth-radius planet on the target star.

reasons.why: Depth changes far beyond errors between sectors (899, 4828, 4426 ppm, chi2 49.88 dof 2), inconsistent with a planet on the target.
Variation persists even within one pipeline (TESS-SPOC: 899 ppm vs 4426 ppm, p_constant 1.315e-08) — not calibration between QLP and SPOC.
Individual transits also inconsistent (chi2 54.447 dof 3) with one shallow event at 465 ppm (-4.0 sigma), share_of_top_3 0.994; signal driven by a few events, not steady.
Four stars within 1 TESS pixel could reproduce the dip with <=25% eclipses, plausible_within_1px 4, consistent with blended binary variability.
No sector with a clear difference image so on-target cannot be confirmed; combined with variable depth and high spot amplitude 5415 ppm at 8.523 d supports spots/blend over planet.
